newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka prime minister admitted to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka prime minister admitted to hospital.

text.p: Sri Lankan Prime Minister Sirima Bandaranaike was recovering in a government hospital after being treated for an unspecified ailment, doctors and officials said on Tuesday.
"The prime minister is undergoing treatment. She is recovering well," a senior doctor at Colombo's Sri Jayewardenepura hospital told Reuters.
Bandaranaike, who turns 81 in April, was admitted to hospital late on Monday and would undergo a series of tests, said the doctor, who asked not to be identified.
"She has gone in for a check up and would resume work in a couple of days," an official at the prime minister's residence told Reuters.

Bandaranaike earned a place in history when she became the world's first woman prime minister in 1960 after leading her assassinated husband Solomon Bandaranaike's Sri Lanka Freedom Party to election victory.
She became prime minister for the third time when the People's Alliance led by President Chandrika Kumaratunga, her daughter, won the 1994 general elections.

Frail and in poor health, Bandaranaike was last seen in public at last weekend's funeral of ruling coalition lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala, killed in election campaign-related violence on February 11. Lcoal-level elections are set for March 27.
